1. The present appeal under Section 173 read with Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles

sentences.text: On 01.01.2008 at about 7:00 p.m., deceased Fatehsinh Mahiji Parmar was riding his Hero Puch Home and was plying his Hero Puch on the left hand side of the road at a moderate speed.

When he reached near Timba na Muvada, at that time, the driver of the offending tractor bearing registration No.GJ-7- AN-3013 along with Trailer bearing registration No.GJ-7-UU- 1557 came from the opposite side very rashly and negligently with excessive speed and dashed with the said Hero Puch bike of the deceased, due to which, deceased fell down on the road and the wheel of the said Tailer ran over him as a result of which Fatehsinh had sustained serious injuries and died on the spot.
2.2 Thereafter, the son of the deceased, namely, Ajaykumar lodged a complaint before the Thermal O.P., Thasra Police Station being I-C.R.No.1/2008.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/06/2023 undefined 2.3

Thereafter, the heirs and legal representatives of the deceased preferred a claim petition being M.A.C.P. No.260 of 2008, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-
2.4
Thereafter, during the pendency of the claim petition, the driver of the offending vehicle was expired and his name was deleted by an order passed below Exh.76.

2.5 Summons came to be issued to the owner of the vehicle and he appeared through his advocate and filed written statement vide Exh.15 contending that during the period when the said incident Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co ... vs Ishwarbhai Somabhai Vankar (Deleted) on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97627663/
2 took place, the offending vehicles were validly under insurance cover of Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. and, therefore, owner is not liable to pay any compensation.

sentences.text: 2.6 The Tribunal vide impugned judgment and award dated 18.04.2011, awarded compensation of Rs.13,08,600/- with simple interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the realization.
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award, the Insurance Company is here before this Court with the present appeal.

3. Learned advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati appearing on behalf of the appellant-opponent No.3 Insurance Company has submitted that the judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is unjust, improper and contrary to law and the conclusion arrived at by the learned Tribunal is erroneous one and against the provisions of law and, therefore, the same is required to be quashed and set aside by allowing the present NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2011 JUDGMENT DATED:
20/06/2023 undefined first appeal.

Learned advocate Mr. Nanavati has submitted that it is an admitted position of fact that the driver who was driving the tractor along with the trolley for unloading 'dried grain' was not having the valid and effective driving license to drive the transport vehicle as he was carrying goods and not agricultural equipment in the trolley.
Learned advocate Mr.

Nanavati has submitted that the driving license of the driver is part and parcel of the record and bare perusal of the driving license itself shows and suggests that the said license was issued by the concerned RTO for the period between 2 nd December, 1996 and 1 st December, 2016.
In short, the duration of the period of driving license is twenty years.
Therefor, it can be said that the driver was holding the driving license for non-transporting vehicles and entitled to drive the non-transport vehicles during that period.
Nowhere in the driving license, endorsement of transport vehicle is made by the office of the RTO.

If the driver of the tractor and trolley was having effective driving license to drive transport vehicle, in that event, period of the driving license would be of three years,
and after lapse of every three years, once again after clearing all the requisite requirements of driving license, endorsement and seal from the office of RTO is required to be affixed on the driving license.

Admittedly, the said endorsement is not there in the driving license and, therefore, it can be safely said that the driver of the tractor and trolley was not holding valid and effective driving license and in the absence of valid and effective driving license, if any vehicle is being driven by the driver, in that event, the insurance company cannot be held liable to indemnify the amount of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/06/2023 undefined compensation of the claimants and solely on this ground, the insurance company is required to be exonerated from the charges levelled against it.

At the time of issuing policy, the basic condition precedent is laid by the insurance company that the driver of the vehicle should have to possess valid and effective driving license, and in the absence of the same, the insurance company would not be held liable.

Learned advocate Mr. Nanavati has submitted that as per the statutory provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, more particularly, Section 14(2), a transport vehicle license is required to be renewed after every three years.

4. Learned advocate Mr. Nanavati has further submitted that learned Judge ought to have to appreciate the fact that in the order dated 17.12.2009 passed in the review petition filed by the appellant-insurance company against the interim order under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the Tribunal had already come to the conclusion in para-6 that the driver was not possessing Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co ... vs Ishwarbhai Somabhai Vankar (Deleted) on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97627663/
3 valid and effective license.
5.

Learned advocate Mr. Nanavati has submitted that it is an admitted position of fact that tractor along with trolley would fall under the category of transport vehicle and the driver who was not holding the driving license to drive the transport vehicle is not entitled to drive the transport vehicle and, therefore, there is a clear cut breach of the policy condition, and as such, the insurance company is required to be exonerated.
6.

Learned advocate Mr. Paresh M. Darji appearing on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/06/2023 undefined behalf of the original claimants has submitted that the judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal is just, fair and reasonable and based upon the sound principles of law.

Learned advocate Mr. Darji has submitted that the present appeal is filed by the insurance company solely on the ground that the driver of the tractor was not holding and possessing valid and effective driving license.

Mr. Darji has submitted that the driver of the tractor was having the driving license to drive the heavy vehicle and the copy of the driving license was produced by the claimants and in the driving license, it is clearly stated that the holder of the license is competent to drive heavy vehicle for the period between 2 nd December, 1996 and 1st December, 2016.
Learned advocate Mr. Darji has submitted that it is true that the endorsement of transport vehicle is not available in the said license after lapse of initial three years.

Learned advocate Mr. Darji has submitted that the said issue is no longer res integra in view of the decision rendered by the Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663, wherein the larger Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if driver is holding license to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Darji has submitted that the present appeal is preferred by the Insurance Company mainly by raising the ground of non-availability of valid and effective driving license by the driver at the time of the incident.

Thus, it is submitted that considering the principles enunciated by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2011 JUDGMENT DATED:
20/06/2023 undefined Hon'ble Apex Court in the above referred judgment, the present appeal lacks merit and is required to be dismissed by confirming the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
7.

Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the respective parties and considering the controversy involved in the present case which is in a very narrow compass, it appears that the insurance company has challenged the judgment and award solely on the ground that the driver of the tractor was not holding valid and effective driving license.

The insurance company empathetically submitted that the driving license produced by the claimants itself shows and suggests that the driving license is effective for the period of twenty years instead of three years.

If the driver was holding valid and effective driving license, in that event, the concerned RTO would have issued the driving license for the period of three years and/or if the driving license is issued for the period of twenty years, in that event, the concerned driver has to pay visit to the office of the RTO after lapse of three years and have to get endorsement upon the driving license that he was having skill to drive the transport vehicle

and this is the statutory requirement on the part of RTO to verify the driving skill of the person as per the relevant provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act and Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co ... vs Ishwarbhai Somabhai Vankar (Deleted) on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97627663/
4

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co ... vs Ishwarbhai Somabhai Vankar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: after verifying and scrutinizing the driving skill of the driver, a noting in the form of an endorsement is to be made in the driving license after lapse of every three years and if driver fails to obtain such an endorsement upon the driving license, in that event, it would become non-effective and can be said that the driver was not holding and possessing NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/06/2023 undefined the driving license to drive the vehicle, and in absence thereof, the Insurance Company should not be saddled with the liability.
The issue involved in the present first appeal revolves around the validity of the driving license of the driver who was driving the tractor trolley at the time of incident.

The present case also stands covered by the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra), wherein in the Hon'ble Apex Court has held thus;
"58.
Transport vehicle has been defined in section 2(47) of the Act, to mean a public service vehicle, a goods carriage, an educational institution bus or a private service vehicle.

Public service vehicle has been defined in section 2(35) to mean any motor vehicle used or adapted to be used for the carriage of passengers for hire or reward and includes a maxicab, a motor cab, contract carriage, and stage carriage.

Goods carriage which is also a transport vehicle is defined in section 2(14) to mean a motor vehicle constructed or adapted for use solely for the carriage of goods, or any motor vehicle not so constructed or adapted when used for the carriage of goods.

It was rightly submitted that a person holding licence to drive light motor vehicle registered for private use, who is driving a similar vehicle which is registered or insured, for the purpose of carrying passengers for hire or reward, would not require an endorsement as to drive a transport vehicle, as the same is not contemplated by the provisions of the Act.
It was also rightly contended that there are several vehicles which can be used for private use as well as for carrying passengers for hire or reward.

When a driver is authorised to drive a vehicle, he can drive it irrespective of the fact whether it is used for a private purpose or for purpose of hire or reward or for carrying the goods in the said vehicle.
It is what is intended by the provision of the Act, and the Amendment Act 54/1994.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/06/2023 undefined 59. Section 10 of the Act requires a driver to hold a licence with respect to the class of vehicles and not with respect to the type of vehicles.
In one class of vehicles, there may be different kinds of vehicles.
If they fall in the same class of vehicles, no separate endorsement is required to drive such vehicles.
As light motor vehicle includes transport vehicle also, a holder of light motor vehicle licence can drive all the vehicles of the class including transport vehicles.
It was pre-amended position as well the post-amended position of Form 4 as amended on 28.3.2001.

Any other interpretation would be repugnant to the definition of "light motor vehicle" in section 2(21) and the provisions of section 10(2)(d), Rule 8 of the Rules of 1989, other provisions and also the forms which are in tune with the provisions.

Even otherwise the forms never intended to exclude transport vehicles from the category of 'light Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co ... vs Ishwarbhai Somabhai Vankar (Deleted) on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97627663/
5 motor vehicles' and for light motor vehicle, the validity period of such licence hold good and apply for the transport vehicle of such class also and the expression in Section 10(2)(e) of the Act 'Transport Vehicle' would include medium goods vehicle,
medium passenger motor vehicle, heavy goods vehicle, heavy passenger motor vehicle which earlier found place in section 10(2)(e) to (h)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
and our conclusion is fortified by the syllabus and rules which we have discussed.
60.

Thus we answer the questions which are referred to us thus:
60.1 'Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).

Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act No.54/1994.
60.2

A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2257/2011 JUDGMENT DATED:
20/06/2023 undefined 7500 kg. would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form.

60.3 The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f), heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)(h) with expression 'transport vehicle'
as substituted in section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.

It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(2)
(d) and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

60.4 The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle"
continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."

sentences.text: In view of the above settled legal position, the decision of the Tribunal while partly allowing the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 cannot be faulted with since the issue is no longer res integra and is squarely covered in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra).

In this case also, the Tribunal while partly allowing the claim petition has observed that the driver having a license to drive the light motor vehicle would be deemed to have the authority to drive transport vehicle not exceeding 7500 Kgs.
9.
In the result, this appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
